scenario.summary: Threat actors utilized vishing to impersonate IT help desks and establish remote sessions via Microsoft Quick Assist, or exploited CVE-2023-20198 on Cisco IOS XE edge devices to gain entry. Post-compromise, they deployed RMM tools and vulnerable drivers to terminate EDR systems (BYOVD) before conducting multi-day data exfiltration via Rclone and deploying ransomware variants like VYPR and Interlock.

meta.rationale: The analyst focuses on high-value endpoints where the adversary might have cleared security logs. Prioritize servers and workstations showing recent administrative tool usage or PowerShell activity.

hunt.name: EDR Impairment and RMM-Driven Ransomware Execution
hunt.description: This hunt targets the execution and defense evasion stages observed in Q3 2026 ransomware campaigns, such as VYPR and Interlock. It identifies the direct impairment of security agents like Cisco Secure Endpoint and the Windows System File Checker (sfc.exe). The hunt corroborates these leads by detecting kernel driver stacking—a signature of BYOVD experimentation—and the deployment of RMM tools used for PowerShell-based MSI installations. An agent weighs the combined evidence of control disruption and suspicious deployment to identify hosts at immediate risk of impact.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, process_cmd_line, parent_process_name, user_name, time FROM hb_process_activity WHERE ((activity_id = 2 AND (instr(',' || '{{security_processes}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(process_name) || ',') > 0 OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%\\cscm.exe' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%\\sfc.exe' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%\\msmpeng.exe' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%\\msascuil.exe')) OR (LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%\\taskkill.exe' AND (LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%/f%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%/im%'))) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: The query identifies where the adversary terminated security agents or system integrity tools, a primary indicator of defense evasion.
config.expected_signal: Rows showing the termination of Cisco Secure Endpoint (cscm.exe) or the Windows Defender process. Silence suggests no direct process-level impairment of these targets occurred.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, driver_path, driver_signature_subject, COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY device_hostname) AS load_count, time FROM hb_kernel_extension_activity WHERE activity_id = 1 AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') ORDER BY load_count DESC
config.description: The hunt identifies hosts where the adversary loaded an unusually high number of drivers, indicating a BYOVD attack.
config.expected_signal: A single host with more than 3 unique driver loads in a short window, particularly with non-standard signers. This aligns with VYPR BYOVD tactics.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, message, package_calling_process, time FROM hb_application_lifecycle WHERE (instr(',' || '{{rmm_tools}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(message) || ',') > 0 OR LOWER(message) LIKE '%.msi%') AND (LOWER(package_calling_process) LIKE '%\\powershell.exe' OR LOWER(package_calling_process) LIKE '%\\pwsh.exe') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: The query detects the adversary installing RMM packages or MSI files via PowerShell, as seen in the VYPR campaign.
config.expected_signal: The query finds evidence of the adversary installing MeshAgent or similar RMM tools via PowerShell commands. Silence proves only that no MSI lifecycle events matched the keywords.
